label: sparse token-conjunction: original-phase step ~3 after b/p, first token r/y/d
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps). 83% of its mass is in the original phase, peaking at t=3 (49% of mass) and never firing at t=0 or t=1. It fires very little in the delimiter and copy phases. It looks like several token-identity cues stacking up: previous input b or p (about 10x lift), current input e/j/n/p/i (4-5x), first token r/y/d (5-7x) and the token two back being b (8x). Top examples look like r b b [e], d b b [e], y r w 0 p [p]. No single cue or clean conjunction separates it. A strict AND of the cues reaches precision 0.13-0.48 with recall under 0.2. The best I found was a 4-of-5 vote over the cues (dev F1 0.26, mass recall 0.42). Top-quartile activations are covered somewhat better than low ones. Each cue on its own fires on thousands of steps where the feature is silent, so this is best read as a hidden-state direction that is not interpretable from tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=3 & prev_tok=b (+5.18), t=2 & prev_tok=b (+4.56), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+4.05), prev_tok=p (+3.85), orig0=y (+3.49), phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+3.46). Lower it: prev2_tok=y (-2.95), prev_tok=w (-2.90), prev_tok=y (-2.83), in_tok=w (-2.67).
